eyebrow: SQL for Oracle Financials · Chapter Two
subtitle: Lesson 8 · Joining Financial Tables

code:
SELECT s.vendor_name, i.invoice_num, i.invoice_amount
FROM poz_suppliers s
LEFT OUTER JOIN ap_invoices_all i
    ON s.vendor_id = i.vendor_id;
caption: Every supplier survives, matched or not — unmatched invoice columns come back NULL.

eyebrow: The pattern: outer join, then IS NULL
code:
SELECT s.vendor_name
FROM poz_suppliers s
LEFT OUTER JOIN ap_invoices_all i
    ON s.vendor_id = i.vendor_id
WHERE i.invoice_id IS NULL;
caption: Only suppliers with zero matching invoices survive this filter.

code:
SELECT i.invoice_num, i.invoice_amount
FROM ap_invoices_all i
LEFT OUTER JOIN ap_invoice_payments_all ip
    ON ip.invoice_id = i.invoice_id
WHERE ip.invoice_id IS NULL;
caption: Every invoice that has never had a single payment applied.
The (+) pre-ANSI syntax — still seen in older code, harder to read, easy to misplace.
